intro: A progressive acoustic outfit from Portland.
story: Cross-Eyed Rosie, a progressive acoustic band that grew out of guitarist Jon Ostrom's weekly coffee-shop gig with friends, formed in Portland in 2002 and played Pickathon in 2004 and again in 2008. Bluegrass roots met pop, jazz and funk on Lookin' Up in 2004 and Adjusted in 2007, both on their own Uncle Ostrom Records. The band later quietly disbanded.
artist_reel_line: Lookin' Up and Adjusted came out on their own Uncle Ostrom Records.

intro: A Portland folk duo of Keeley Boyle and Nelson Kempf.
story: The Old Believers, the Portland folk duo of Keeley Boyle and Nelson Kempf, both about 19 or 20 and raised in Alaska, played Pickathon in 2008 with a lineup that could swell to a dozen. Eight Golden Greats, on Fine/Romantic Recordings that year, moved them from folk-pop into uncharted territory, in Willamette Week's words. They stepped away from active touring in the years that followed.
artist_reel_line: They stepped back from active touring after Eight Golden Greats.

intro: An Austin punk-grass band led by banjoist Danny Barnes.
story: Bad Livers, the Austin band led by banjoist Danny Barnes, began around March 1990 as the Danny Barnes Trio, with Mark Rubin on bass and tuba and Ralph White III on fiddle and accordion, mixing bluegrass with punk speed. Delusions of Banjer came out on Quarterstick in 1992, and Blood and Mood followed in 2000, when the original lineup ended. Barnes and Rubin, with Bob Grant, played reunion shows in 2008, the year of Pickathon, then in 2009 and 2014, and Barnes keeps working as a solo artist.
artist_reel_line: Co-founder Danny Barnes keeps working as a solo artist.

intro: A Portland chamber-folk collective led by Ritchie Young.
story: Loch Lomond began in 2003 as Ritchie Young's solo recording and grew into a Portland chamber-folk collective, a rising local favorite when it played Pickathon in 2008, a year after Paper the Walls on Hush. Little Me Will Start a Storm came out on Tender Loving Empire in February 2011 and in the UK on the Scottish label Chemikal Underground, which also released Dresses in 2013. The band toured internationally.
artist_reel_line: Dresses came out on Chemikal Underground in 2013.

intro: A DIY folk-rock veteran with an Atlantic debut.
story: Melissa Ferrick, from Ipswich, Massachusetts, went from a Berklee scholarship to a deal with Atlantic at 21, after opening for Morrissey. Massive Blur came out in 1993, and she played Pickathon in 2008, long after going independent with her own Right On Records. She later taught songwriting and the music business at Berklee and then Northeastern, while booking artists and playing East Coast shows, and signed to Kill Rock Stars in 2023.
artist_reel_line: She signed to Kill Rock Stars in 2023.

intro: A Portland guitarist from the Northwest bluegrass circuit.
story: Scott Law, a Portland guitarist who has been a professional since 1992 and toured with Melvin Seals and Hanuman before forming the Scott Law Band, played Pickathon in 2008 and shared a set with fiddler Darol Anger. He has stayed a versatile collaborator in Portland, and in late 2026 he was mixing a new ten-song album.
artist_reel_line: He was mixing a new ten-song album in late 2026.

story: The Gourds formed in Austin in the summer of 1994 around Kevin Russell, Jimmy Smith, Claude Bernard and drummer Charlie Llewellin, and made Dem's Good Beeble in 1996. They played Pickathon in 2008, a year after a first visit, with Haymaker! on Yep Roc a year away. The Americana Music Association nominated "Country Love" for Song of the Year in 2009. After Old Mad Joy in 2011 the band went on hiatus in late 2013 while Russell led Shinyribs, and in May 2026 it reunited for two shows at Austin's Paramount Theatre.
artist_reel_line: The band reunited for two shows at Austin's Paramount Theatre in May 2026.

intro: An Irish button-accordion player with a Portland following.
story: Johnny B. Connolly, a Dublin-born button accordionist, came to Portland on a 1997 tour and stayed. His friendship with the fiddler Kevin Burke led to a deal with Green Linnet in 2001 and his debut, Bridgetown, named for his adopted hometown. He played Pickathon in 2008, one of three visits, and still tours the West with his own trio and with longtime collaborators such as Tony Furtado, including a September 2026 show in Fort Collins, Colorado.
artist_reel_line: He played Fort Collins, Colorado, with Tony Furtado in September 2026.
